chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil ibn Baziʿ, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymun, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid, who said:

I asked Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about the leper and the one afflicted with vitiligo leading the Muslims in prayer. He said: “Yes.” I said: “Does Allah test the believer by means of them?” He said: “Yes; and was tribulation written for anyone except the believer?”

So the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it as applying to a state of necessity in which no one suitable for the Imamate of prayer is found except one with this description. And it is possible that the meaning in it is permissibility, even though the merit is in the first division.

key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: a state of necessity requiring legal allowance
key_terms.الْأَبْرَصِ: a person afflicted with vitiligo or a visible skin condition
key_terms.الْبَلَاءُ: tribulation or trial decreed as a test
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer who is subject to divine testing
key_terms.يَؤُمَّانِ: they lead others in congregational salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Can a person afflicted with leprosy or vitiligo lead the Muslims in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the permissibility of a leper or a person afflicted with vitiligo leading the Muslims in salat (prayer). The Imam عليه السلام affirms the possibility and links such conditions to divine trial for the believer, while the closing legal note explains the report as applying especially in necessity, though permissibility may still be understood more generally.
